1.text: Labour, "anxiety," ascolia. M. --- All misery (C.) is in consequence of original sin. W. --- The life of man is a trial. Job vii. 1. and xiv. 1. --- Of all. The earth, (C.) which covers us, when all other things cast us away. Pliny ii. 63.

4.text: Purple. Lit. "hyacinth," (H.) or violet colour. Purple was more like scarlet.

5.text: Knowledge. He is disquieted by restless (C.) and frightful dreams. v. 6. H.

7.text: Fear, or no reason for it. C.

8.text: Beast. Their instinct causes them to fear death, to fight, &c.

9.text: Moreover. Gr. "death," &c. are all destined for the wicked.

12.text: Out, and severely punished. C. --- They shall not appear in the book of life.

14.text: Rejoice. The corrupt judge once rejoiced: but now he shall mourn. H. --- The possessions and grandeur of the unjust shall end in a moment, like a clap of thunder. Ps. xxxvi. 36. Prov. x. 25. C.

15.text: And make. Gr. "they are unclean," (H.) and will produce no fruit.

16.text: Weed. Lit. "verdure." Gr. Achei, (H.) properly denotes the rush, papyrus, which grows on the banks of the Nile, (Gen. xli. 2. C.) and was used for fuel. Alpin. i. 7. Matt. vi. 30. --- Thus the wicked will presently (C.) be treated. M.

17.text: Grace. The beneficent will produce fruits, like those of paradise. Gen. ii. 8.

18.text: That is. Gr. "and of one that." --- In it. Gr. "and more than both is one discovering a treasure," (H.) who finds himself rich, without labour or injustice.

19.text: Both. Thus Judith, Zenobia, &c. ennobled their husbands. Prov. xxxi. 10.

20.text: Wisdom. Virtue gives more content to the soul than corporal pleasures do to the body. It brings us near to God. C.

22.text: Green. "The sight of no colour is more agreeable to the eyes." Pliny xxxvii. 1. --- The Church is more excellent than the synagogue. W.

23.text: Husband. Their union is closer, and they can best assist each other.

25.text: Counsel. By this the Romans conquered the world. 1 Mac. viii. 31. Prov. xi. 14.

26.text: Heart, and make people presumptuous; while piety gives real courage. Ps. xxvi. 1. C.

28.text: It, or "him." H. --- The virtuous man is covered with glory.

29.text: Indigent. Gr. "live not by begging," being too lazy to work, or incurring this punishment for thy sins. Lev. xxvi. 16. Ps. cviii. Deut. xv. 4. Involuntary poverty is a most severe scourge. C. --- All are bound too labour for what is needful; (W.) some by prayer, others by trade, &c. H.

30.text: Meat. Such is the condition of the parasite, (C.) and of the beggar. H.

32.text: Unwise. Some read, "impudent man," with the Gr. --- Fire. He shall feel the inconveniences of poverty; (H.) yet will not work, being lost to all shame. C. --- Plato (Leg. 11.) orders magistrates to "clear the country of such an animal," zwou, (H.) and the Lacedemonians suffered no beggars among them.
